# Section 05 Highlights

## Highlight 1
**Headline:** eCat is the primary transaction system — 131% GMV capture ($10.1M vs $7.8M total business)
**Context:** eCat processes more orders (1,961) than the total business channel records (1,382). The platform is no longer a supplement — it IS the ordering system. This strengthens the case for investing in catalog completeness and rep tooling.
**Section:** [§5 Commerce Analytics](#commerce)

## Highlight 2
**Headline:** Top 3 reordering accounts showing 25–36% price erosion — potential trade-down pattern
**Context:** Robb & Stucky (-35.9%), CAI Designs (-31.0%), and Loeffler (-25.7%) are all shifting toward lower average item prices. These are your most frequent orderers, so the margin impact compounds. Worth investigating whether this reflects deliberate product mix shifts or pricing pressure.
**Section:** [§5 Commerce Analytics](#commerce)
**Priority Action Candidate:** YES
**Urgency:** MEDIUM — Not immediate revenue loss, but compounding margin pressure on your most active accounts.

## Highlight 3
**Headline:** Quote orders average $10,674 — 2.3× the confirmed order AOV — $2.1M in pipeline value
**Context:** 193 quotes at premium AOV suggest the quote workflow is used for larger, multi-item proposals. Tracking quote-to-order conversion and accelerating follow-up on open quotes could materially increase revenue.
**Section:** [§5 Commerce Analytics](#commerce)

## Highlight 4
**Headline:** SOFAS category declined 24% and CAT20 dropped 41% half-over-half
**Context:** SOFAS fell from $160K to $121K and CAT20 from $113K to $67K. Since all categories show 100% eCat share, these are genuine demand declines rather than channel shifts. CAT8 (+78.6%) and CAT21 (+395%) are growing rapidly, suggesting a portfolio mix evolution.
**Section:** [§5 Commerce Analytics](#commerce)
